page: Amazon Web Services a1.4xlarge is an ARM-based compute instance built on the first-generation AWS Graviton processor and the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The server delivers 16 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz using Cortex-A72 ARMv8 cores with one thread per core. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB of RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU, while network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The instance does not bundle integrated local storage or GPU hardware.

Synthetic CPU benchmarks demonstrate steady multi-threaded throughput alongside lower single-threaded metrics. In stress-ng evaluations, single-core and multi-core CPU performance place in the middle 50% average range, supported by Clang software compilation and ray tracing scores in Geekbench that also reach average tiers. However, instruction throughput in PassMark yields weak results, with overall CPU and memory benchmark scores settling in the bottom 25%. Geekbench single-core performance ranks in the bottom 10% at 409.0, reflecting the architectural limitations of older Cortex-A72 microarchitecture.

Memory subsystem metrics indicate substantial performance differences between cache tiers. Cached read bandwidth reaches an average 566.18 GB/sec, but uncached read operations fall to 32.43 GB/sec and uncached write operations register at 10.01 GB/sec, placing memory write speeds in the bottom 10%. Real-world application throughput aligns with these characteristics: Redis SET operations sustain an average 8.36 million operations per second and database operations score in the average tier, while single-threaded data compression and decompression workloads exhibit poor performance.

Given the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and multi-threaded scaling efficiency, this server configuration fits scale-out web serving, multi-threaded container workloads, Redis caching tiers, and software build pipelines optimized for arm64 execution.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.4xlarge is an ARM-based compute instance powered by first-generation AWS Graviton processors with 16 dedicated Cortex-A72 cores running at 2.3 GHz. Configured under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core, alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark assessments, the instance achieves average results in stress-ng multi-core tests, software compilation, and Redis SET operations reaching 8.36 million operations per second. However, single-core metrics and uncached memory write bandwidth rank in the lower percentiles due to first-generation ARMv8 architecture limits. With dedicated physical cores and consistent multi-threaded compute, the server is suitable for arm64-compatible scale-out workloads, caching clusters, software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices.
